item.title: Renormalisation Group V: Wilson's Momentum Shells
item.description: Part 5 of the renormalisation group course. From spins to a smooth field, Wilson's three-step RG in momentum space explained as filtering music and zooming out, the free-field (Gaussian) fixed point, power counting and why four dimensions is special.

item.title: Renormalisation Group IV: Fixed Points and Universality
item.description: Part 4 of the renormalisation group course. What a critical point looks like, why it is a fixed point of the RG, relevant and irrelevant directions as a ball on a mountain ridge, critical exponents from one number, universality as a river basin and the exact 2D critical temperature from a mirror symmetry. Then the exponents are measured properly, by finite-size scaling of Wolff cluster simulations: the Binder crossing gives K_c to 0.02 per cent where the pencil method is 31 per cent off. With a live 2D Ising simulation you can coarse-grain.

item.title: Renormalisation Group III: Block Spins
item.description: Part 3 of the renormalisation group course. Kadanoff's block-spin idea done exactly on a line of spins, explained as a game of telephone: the recursion tanh K' = tanh^2 K, fixed points and a correlation length that never changes when you measure it properly. With an interactive widget.

item.title: The Renormalisation Group: a beginner's course
item.description: An eight-part beginner's course on the renormalisation group, in simple words with an everyday picture for every idea: loops and cutoffs from scratch, block spins and the Ising chain, fixed points and universality, Wilson's momentum shells, the Wilson-Fisher fixed point, running couplings in QED and QCD, then effective field theory. Every formula checked in Wolfram and FORM, with live simulations in the browser.
